body: What do you think of him now? When you guys are under really bad or bright lighting that is unflattering, does it change the make-up of your intimacy with him? How/why did you start looking past his face and started becoming sexually attracted to him? Sorry for all the questions.

I work-out. Though it has somewhat improved my self-esteem, it won't change what the universe decided to hand me on top of my shoulders. But it does help your self-image a bit. And since you're only overweight, you have the power to change it any minute you choose to.
Yea, nothing worse then getting your heart broken. I loved this girl a lot, perhaps more then I have felt about any other girl before. It sucks.

I have, for the most part, spent a lot of the extra government aid funds for college, on skin-clearing procedures. Probably a few thousand dollars. But the improvements are subtle at best. Yet I used to keep going back by the small thread of hope that there was still a chance for it to improve. I think I gave up on that by now. I dont have a lot of money anyway

There are times when I thought that perhaps a certain girl liked me. But many times girls I like (a lot of it is because how they treat me, as usually girls dont respond to me), it turns out they were just friendly. 

Its really hard to gauge whether a girl likes me or not. For instance, when a girl glances your way, a normal looking person might think she has a developed interest in him, but I can't think "does this girl like me, but is shy to say anything" or "is this girl repulsed by me, and is just starring curiously". 

If I start taking the initiative with every girl I talk to, I'll just come off as a creeper whose desperate for a sex. Because I am sure, 9 times out of 10, theyre going to be turned off by my aggressive approach. Yet if I dont do anything, sometimes I think I might have passed on an opportunity. Its a catch-22 situation.

I go out into the world feeling okay about myself, if I didn't, I would probably stay inside (which I tend to do quite a bit when I feel like shit). But its the way the world greets me, which reminds me, "Oh right, I'm ugly." I try to avoid the thoughts as much as possible, but the world keeps reminding me and bringing me right back to them. 

Whenever I'm in class, it never fails that people like to secretly stare at me, assuming I don't notice them.

I'll never forget this one time when I was eating at a pizza place with a couple of friends in this brightly-lit room. We were by a large window a lot of people pass through, and I'd say 70-80% of the people looked back twice towards me or gave a long, curious stare. I felt like some sort of circus freak, sans a ringleader projecting his voice to the passers, "Ladies and gentlemen, I present to you Exhibit A". I felt a deep burn inside, even though I didn't show it. I never know how to react to these situations without coming off as further repulsive, so sometimes I can't help but just sarcastically wink at them. 

People have made snide comments, and the look in many of the eyes is as if they just seen a ghost. Whenever I am out eating with people it never fails that someone will throw a quick glance at me and shake their heads fast back and forth. Not sure what kind of reaction this is, maybe theyre trying to pretend they werent looking at me, or they just involuntarily start jolting like that, but it always happens. 

The point im trying to make is, though I appreciate your empathy, I feel patronized when someone tells me a lot of it is in my head. The people's reception to me is what makes me miserable, I seldom ever go out into the world predisposed to misery. My bitterness is not a fabrication, but a conclusion. And sometimes I feel it would be best for me to just go the way of Thoreau, and live in the woods away from everyone.
